source: TomorrowX Summit (iConnections) — Opening session: retail as most powerful market force, AI buildout railroad vs telecom, P(doom) vs P(boom)
summary: Zero interest rate environment would have caused a dangerous AI overbuild; higher real rates and supply constraints are preventing this
summary_extended: Baker argues that the current AI infrastructure buildout is structurally protected from a catastrophic overbuild cycle precisely because interest rates are elevated and physical supply constraints (power/watts, wafers, and HBM capacity) are binding. He contrasts this with a hypothetical zero interest rate environment, where he claims TSMC, Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix would be expanding capacity by 200%, which — based on 400 years of capitalist history — would guarantee a ruinous overbuild. The investment implication is that current constraints act as a circuit breaker, making the AI buildout more analogous to a disciplined infrastructure cycle than the speculative telecom bubble of the late 1990s. Baker presents this as a high-conviction structural observation: the combination of higher real rates and physical bottlenecks in wafers and power is what separates this cycle from prior boom-bust patterns in semiconductors and infrastructure.
detail: Baker explicitly contrasts the current environment with a hypothetical ZIRP world where TSMC, Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix would be expanding capacity 200%, guaranteeing an overbuild. He cites this as the historical pattern of 400 years of capitalism. Current constraints (rates, watts, wafers) are the circuit breaker.
confidence_evidence: Baker states this as a structural historical observation with high conviction; names specific companies as examples

ticker_audit.reasoning: TSMC is explicitly named by Baker as one of the companies that would be expanding wafer capacity 200% in a ZIRP world; it is a direct subject of the capacity discipline thesis and a direct beneficiary of the constrained, non-overbuild environment.

Micron is explicitly named by Baker as a company that would be dangerously overbuilding in a ZIRP environment; as the only US-listed HBM/DRAM producer, it is a direct subject of this supply constraint thesis and benefits from the disciplined capacity environment.
